The *Lakuṇḍakabhaddiyattheragāthā* (Thag 7.2) is a poetic discourse belonging to the *Theragāthā* collection, attributed to the elder Lakuṇḍaka Bhaddiya [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into multiple modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato, as part of nine translations across eight languages recorded on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

The text exhibits extensive internal and cross-tradition parallels corroborated by curated records and computational text-reuse analysis [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali Canon, verses corresponding to segments §4.1–7.5 share substantial material with the *Rūpasutta* (AN 4.65) in the *Catukkanipāta*, and verses §3.3–7.5 are cited and commented upon in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Beyond the Pali tradition, curated parallels include the *Śrutavarga* chapter of the *Udānavarga* in Sanskrit (including the Subaši recension), the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (*Uv Kg* 22), and Chinese translations (T 212.23 and T 213.22), as well as the Sanskrit *Śarīrārthagāthā* [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus additionally identifies lower-scoring cross-language alignments with Tibetan versions of the *Yogācārabhūmi* (D4035) and the *Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* (D0012) [DharmaNexus].
